classification.difficultyReason: Solve the straight-angle equation and compare the resulting alternate angles to decide parallelism.

inlines.text: Show working to explain how you know.

spec.description: Straight segments A–B–C and D–E–F slope gently down to the right. A diagonal transversal rises through E and B and extends past both intersections. Adjacent sectors ABE and EBC below ABC are labelled (5x + 6)° and (16x + 6)°. Sector DEB above DEF is labelled (20x − 15)°. No parallel marks or shading.
spec.mathematics: A,B,C are collinear and D,E,F are collinear. The transversal contains E and B. Angles ABE and EBC form a straight angle. No parallelism is given. Coordinates reproduce the schematic source, not measured angle values.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three supplied angle expressions and point labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Angles on straight line $ABC$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}(5x+6)+(16x+6)&=180\\21x+12&=180\\21x&=168\\x&=8\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\angle EBC&=(16\times8+6)^\circ\\&=134^\circ\\\angle DEB&=(20\times8-15)^\circ\\&=145^\circ\end{align*}$$
The alternate angles are unequal. Therefore $ABC$ is not parallel to $DEF$.
